title: A group's existence is continuous and it never reappears after disappearing

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A group's existence is continuous and it never reappears after disappearing

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Genera and families, like species, exist continuously from their first to last appearance and do not reappear after they have once disappeared, since their members must form an unbroken succession of generations.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. X: On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: A group does not reappear after it has once disappeared; or its existence, as long as it lasts, is continuous.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter X, “On the Geological Succession of Organic Beings”; section “Groups of species follow the same general rules in their appearance and disappearance as do single species”. Scope: genera and families in the fossil record

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch10-05: resolvable-now, resolvability 0.84

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Continuity of higher taxa is directly testable with occurrence ranges and standard gap analyses. The fossil record cannot prove uninterrupted presence everywhere, but broad violations or support are resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For genera and families, identify gaps between dated occurrences and estimate sampling-adjusted probabilities of true absence. Confirm continuity when gap lengths match expected non-detection; validated extinction followed by renewed membership would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Higher-taxon boundaries are revised over time.

Poor sampling can create false disappearance and reappearance.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Genus and family ranges are directly downloadable and better populated than species ranges. The empirical pattern of stratigraphic continuity can be described for marine invertebrates. Sampling gaps, and the shift from Darwin's morphological groups to monophyletic taxa, keep a clean refutation rare.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Measure internal gaps in genus and family ranges and ask whether any group is genuinely absent from a well-sampled interval and then resumes. Persistent occurrence at low density would support continuity; a well-sampled absence followed by return of the same group would challenge it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Lazarus gaps from uneven collecting dominate apparent disappearances and returns.

If groups are treated as clades, continuity through time is close to a definition and the test loses force.
